page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c4.3xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture utilizing an Intel Xeon E5-2667 v4 processor running at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The instance is configured with 12 dedicated physical cores and 12 vCPUs, providing a 1.0 thread-per-core ratio. It is equipped with 24.0 GB of system memory, translating to 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the ecs.c4.3xlarge delivers average multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 8624.76 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 5654.0. Single-core performance is relatively weaker, as shown by a stress-ng single-core score of 1149.99. Memory read bandwidth is average, reaching 620.37 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 52.4 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, though large block write bandwidth is weaker at 24.54 GB/sec. The instance demonstrates stable performance in standard operations, achieving an average of 9.94 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 9.12 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

With its dedicated CPU allocation and 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio, the instance offers a balanced compute-focused profile without the overhead of shared-core resource contention. However, the lack of local storage and GPU acceleration, combined with weak performance in larger workloads like 7B LLM inference, limits its suitability for heavy data science or storage-intensive applications. It is best suited for workloads such as static web serving, software compilation, text processing, and database operations that benefit from dedicated CPU cores but do not require massive memory footprints or local disk storage.
